adversarial_refutations.argument:
NOT REFUTED. I could not construct a checkable case in which CV.SmoothingDefinitionData (statement file 273-371) defines an object other than the printed oriented smoothing / carriers on the printed binder (P diagrammatic, S ∈ Ind(G_P), n ≥ 3).

What I checked, to primitives:
(1) The operation. geoSmoothingSuccessor hP S = ρ ∘ selectedMarkPerm S (SM/FlatCarriersDefs.lean 235-237); selectedMarkPerm S (inr v) = inr (selectedVisitTwin S v), identity on vertices (SM/CarrierSmoothing.lean 36-46); selectedVisitTwin S v = if v.1 ∈ S then visitTwin v else v (SM/CarrierVisitTwin.lean 80-89); visitTwin v = ⟨v.1, other member⟩ (34-35), so v.1.val = {v.2, twin.2} (SM/CarrierCrossings.lean 216-217). ρ = successor in the list of all marks ZMod n ⊕ Visit P sorted by traversalKey = i.val + t (FlatCarriersDefs 127-192, SM/Traversal.lean 17), vertex i at (i,0), visit v at (v.2, crossingParameter) with both visits evaluating to crossingPoint v.1 (SM/GeometricVisits.lean 12-20), which under CrossingGeometry (SM/CrossingGeometry.lean 11-15) is the unique interior transverse common point of two remote closed edges (27-50). Hence ρ_S⁻¹(inr v) = selectedMarkPerm(ρ⁻¹(inr v)) has its plane point on edge v.2 strictly before the crossing (the vertex mark (v.2,0) precedes every visit on that edge, and the list starts at inl 0 with key 0), and ρ_S(inr v) = ρ(inr twin) lies on edge twin.2 strictly after it (a later visit of a different crossing, or the end vertex). So mark v carries the arc "in along d1, out along d2" and its twin "in along d2, out along d1". With the four rays in angular order (+d1,+d2,-d1,-d2) or (+d1,-d2,-d1,+d2) according to sgn det(d1,d2) ≠ 0, the ray pairs {-d1,+d2} and {-d2,+d1} are non-interleaving: this is the unique orientation-respecting non-crossing resolution the print names ("the two arcs that respect the orientation of P and do not cross", excerpt l.3-4); the only other orientation-respecting pairing is the original crossing one. reconnect_selected (278-282) fixes exactly this swap; keep_unselected/keep_vertex (284-290) fix "at each double point of S [only]"; transverse (294-299) certifies the presupposed transversality; oriented_arcs (305-315) certifies incoming ∝ +edge v.2, outgoing ∝ +edge twin.2 with c > 0 (nondegenerate since positions are injective and edges nonzero).
(2) Binder and carrier objects. hD : CV.Diagrammatic P (CV/Setup.lean 1382-1388) is the accepted def:diagrammatic; hD.crossingGeometry (1566) reads the geo layer. Under it the printed double points are exactly Crossing P (SM/Crossings.lean 12-15): a self-intersection is a common point of two distinct closed edges; adjacent edges meet only at their corner under vertex-off (Setup 1399 meet_next_eq_corner, and corners are excluded by clause 4 of Diagrammatic), an edge cannot meet itself (edge ≠ 0), remote pairs meet at a unique interior transverse point, and distinct crossings have distinct points by G2 (crossingPoint_injective_of_geometry, CrossingGeometry.lean 61-80). Each crossing has exactly two visits (SM/GaussVisits.lean 34-36). S ∈ Ind hD.crossingGeometry is the accepted CV:def:interlace on the same hP (CV/Events.lean 165-188), and the carriers GeoComponent = cycles of ρ_S (FlatCarriersDefs 258-264) are the objects of accepted def:flat-carriers, the same SmoothingData words as SM def:smoothing (GeoCarrierSpec 737-802; sm-3:100-113). Domain: the row is on [NeZero n] (198) rather than n ≥ 3; on the printed domain the local ∀ _hn : 3 ≤ n of oriented_arcs (305) and inherited_direction (367) is discharged, so the statement restricted to the printed binder is the full one; the extension to n ∈ {1,2} (no remote edges, hence no visits) is harmless.
(3) Ownership. geoOwner (inr v) is the ρ_S-cycle of inr v, which contains its predecessor on edge v.2: the incoming-visit convention, verbatim sm-3:110-113 ("the node a retains its incoming arc and leaves along the old outgoing arc at b. This also implements the incoming-visit convention explicitly"). The CV text does not fix the assignment of the two preimages: lem:carriers' proof (d1:395-399) reconnects L as L∩α, L∩β without saying where x1, x2 go, and lem:carrierword's proof (d1:465-469) uses the OPEN arcs (c1,c2), (c2,c1). Under either convention the plane curves, the mark sets away from S, and the number of corners per carrier are identical; the Lean turn at mark v (geoInEdge = v.2, geoOutSlot = twin's edge, SM/FlatCarriers.lean 3000-3006, 3020-3038) is the turn of the arc that mark represents, so the convention is internally consistent and matches the AUTHOR_NOTES CV-DOM entry (work/AUTHOR_NOTES.md 3192-3234).
(4) "Disjoint union of closed oriented curves". carriers (325-327) and closed_oriented (330-333) are the cycle model (definitional, FlatCarriersDefs 266-282); disjoint_union (336-341) is the partition of the marks (mem_geoComponentMarkList 294-297), the print's own reading "disjoint as subsets of the traversal circle, not of the plane" (d1:440-444); the mark partition determines the arc partition (the open arc (a, ρa) of Γ is traversed by the cycle of ρa, since ρ_S(σa) = ρa), so the finite model loses nothing. straight_pieces (356-364) and inherited_direction (367-371) make each piece the straight subsegment of the closed original edge of the outgoing slot (geoOutSlot = position of selectedMarkPerm a, FlatCarriers.lean 3000-3002), run in P's direction: the curves are P's own pieces rejoined at the sites, i.e. the printed result.

Reviewer discrepancies: all confirmed real, none blocking. (a) noncrossing_arcs (320-322) is det ≠ 0 (already transverse's 4th conjunct) plus crossingSign_swap (SM/Crossings.lean 83-86, from det_swap SM/Chirotope.lean 30-32); as a proposition it mentions no arc and no ρ_S. But the pair of new arcs is fixed by reconnect_selected and oriented_arcs, and that pair is provably non-crossing (they meet only at the crossing point, with the opposite nonzero turns the field records), so the DEFINED object is the printed one; this is a weak certificate, not a wrong definition. (b) traced_curve (345-352) is the definitional unfolding of geoComponentPlaneCycle (FlatCarriersDefs 310-313, inherited order) and does not itself tie that cycle to the ρ_S-traversal; for a non-independent S they differ, but on the printed binder S ∈ Ind they coincide by the accepted geoTracedSuccessor_of_independent (lem:carrierword), which is correctly not a clause of def:smoothing. (c) _hS unused, the extra structural conjuncts (v.1.val = {v.2, twin.2}, Nodup/nonempty/membership, surjectivity), and the n-domain extension make the Lean stronger, not different. (d) The brief mislocates geoInEdge/geoOutSlot (actually SM/FlatCarriers.lean 3000-3006) and visitTwin (SM/CarrierVisitTwin.lean 34-35); I read exactly those definition lines and the characterising lemma statements, plus the definition lines of Visit, visitParameter (SM/GaussVisits.lean 17, 45-46), geometricVisitPosition (SM/GeometricVisits.lean 12-20), selectedMarkPerm (SM/CarrierSmoothing.lean 36-46), selectedVisitTwin (SM/CarrierVisitTwin.lean 80-89), IsTrueCorner (SM/CarrierTrueCorners.lean 44-54), crossing_other_visit (SM/CrossingPair.lean 27-28), visit_crossing_val_eq_pair (SM/CarrierCrossings.lean 216-217), Mark (SM/CarrierMarks.lean 33), preimages/selfIntersections (CV/Setup.lean 1356-1369) — needed to expand the bundle to primitives; disclosed here. No proofs of the three row theorems were read (statement file only; work/lean/CV/Carriers.lean not opened).

NOT REFUTED. I tried to break the claim that CV.SmoothingDefinitionData (statement file 273-371) with theorem CV.smoothing_definition (374) renders CV:def:smoothing (d1:355-361) on its printed binder, expanding every field to primitives.

1. THE RECONNECTION IS THE PRINTED ONE. geoSmoothingSuccessor hP S = (selectedMarkPerm S).trans (geoMarkSuccessor hP), i.e. ρ_S a = ρ(σ a) (SM/FlatCarriersDefs.lean:235-240); σ(inr v) = inr (visitTwin v) iff v.1 ∈ S else v, σ(inl i) = inl i (SM/CarrierSmoothing.lean:36-46, SM/CarrierVisitTwin.lean:80-88). ρ is cyclic `next` in the list of all marks sorted by traversal key i.val + t (FlatCarriersDefs.lean:127-191, SM/Traversal.lean:17); a visit is positioned at (v.2.val, crossingParameter) with plane point crossingPoint v.1 (SM/GeometricVisits.lean:12-18). Hence for a selected v, ρ_S(inr v) is the mark after twin v on the original circle, on the twin's edge beyond the crossing point: the arc arriving at v along +edge(v.2) leaves along +edge(twin.2). With det(edge v.2, edge twin.2) ≠ 0 (CrossingGeometry clause 2, SM/CrossingGeometry.lean:13-14; twin's edge is the other member of the pair, transverse conj. 1) the four rays at the crossing point are cyclically out_v, out_tw, in_v, in_tw (or its mirror), so {in_v,out_tw}, {in_tw,out_v} are non-interleaving: the swap is the unique orientation-respecting non-crossing resolution and the identity pairing is the crossing one. reconnect_selected (278-282) is definitional (FlatCarriersDefs.lean:245-255); keep_unselected/keep_vertex (284-290) say "and only there". ρ(twin v) ≠ v and ρ(v) ≠ twin v since remote edges are separated by at least one vertex mark, so the swap is nontrivial.

2. ORIENTATION AND TURN SIGNS. oriented_arcs (305-315): the incoming displacement at v is a positive multiple of edge v.2 — I checked the subtle case where ρ⁻¹(inr v) is itself a selected visit w on edge v.2 (then ρ_S⁻¹(inr v) = σ(ρ⁻¹ v) = inr(twin w), whose plane point equals w's, so the displacement is (t_v − t_w)·edge v.2 with t_v > t_w); the outgoing displacement is pos(ρ(twin v)) − crossingPoint = positive multiple of edge twin.2 (next mark on that edge or its end vertex, edgePoint e' 1 = P(e'+1), SM/Polygon.lean:49-55). inherited_direction (367-371) and straight_pieces (356-364) follow from geoOutSlot hP S a = geoMarkPosition hP (σ a) (SM/FlatCarriers.lean:3000-3002; characterisations 3017-3030) and geoSmoothingSegment's definition (FlatCarriersDefs.lean:317-321; straight_pieces conj. 1 is rfl).

3. STRONGEST REFUTATION CANDIDATE, REJECTED. noncrossing_arcs (320-322) unfolds to sign det(d_v,d_tw) ≠ 0 ∧ sign det(d_tw,d_v) = −sign det(d_v,d_tw) (crossingSign, SM/Crossings.lean:80-81; crossingSign_swap 83-86; det_swap SM/Chirotope.lean:30-32). Conjunct 1 repeats transverse conj. 4 (299); conjunct 2 is universally valid; the field mentions neither ρ_S nor the arcs and is equally true of the crossing (identity) pairing — so, alone, it does not certify "do not cross". But the bundle as a whole does: reconnect_selected fixes the swap and oriented_arcs fixes in = +d_v, out = +d_tw at v (the identity pairing would give out = +d_v, contradicting oriented_arcs because d_v ∦ d_tw). Given these, the turn of the new arc at v is sign det(d_v,d_tw) ≠ 0 and at twin v the opposite sign, which at a transverse site is exactly local non-crossing (touching resolution — the same finite-model reading as the accepted SM def:smoothing, sm-3-statesum.tex:100-113). The printed clause's content is carried, redistributed over reconnect_selected + oriented_arcs + noncrossing_arcs; this is a labelling weakness (the docstring 316-319 overstates the field), not a fidelity failure. Non-blocking, agreeing with all three reviewers.

4. CARRIERS / DISJOINT UNION / CURVES. carriers (325-327) is geoOwner_eq_iff (FlatCarriersDefs.lean:258-268: GeoComponent = quotient by SameCycle of ρ_S); closed_oriented (330-333) = geoOwner_successor + geoOwner_surjective (270-282); disjoint_union (336-341) is the partition of marks via geoComponentMarkList = filter of the sorted mark list by owner (290-297) — disjointness on the traversal circle is the paper's own gloss (d1:437-444). traced_curve (345-352) is rfl for geoComponentPlaneCycle (310-313) plus Nodup/length/membership (299-306); it names the curve in INHERITED order while straight_pieces uses ρ_S order — their agreement is lem:carrierword (d1:450-456) / the accepted TracedSuccessor, correctly not a clause of def:smoothing. Extra Lean clauses (keep_*, traced_curve, straight_pieces, inherited_direction, transverse conj. 1-3) are true, explicit renderings of implicit printed content; none asserts anything false or absent from the printed construction.

5. BINDER / DOMAIN. hD : CV.Diagrammatic P (CV/Setup.lean:1382-1388; hD.crossingGeometry 1566), hS : S ∈ Ind hD.crossingGeometry with Ind = independent sets of geometricInterlacementGraph incl. ∅ (CV/Events.lean:165-188; SM/GeometricInterlacement.lean:16-34) — the printed "For S ∈ Ind(G_P)" under the standing diagrammatic hypothesis (lem:carriers d1:362-365 confirms genericity is not assumed). `_hS` is unused: the bundle holds for every S (Lean stronger, harmless). [NeZero n] vs printed n ≥ 3: Diagrammatic is unsatisfiable at n = 1 (IsPolygon needs edge P 0 = P 0 − P 0 ≠ 0, Setup.lean:45, 1383) and at n = 2 (the traversal doubles back along one segment, infinitely many self-intersections against Setup.lean:1384), so the local `3 ≤ n` guards in oriented_arcs/inherited_direction lose nothing on the row's actual domain. Under Diagrammatic the double points of P are exactly the remote-pair crossings (Crossing P, SM/Crossings.lean:12-15; adjacent edges meet only at their corner, Setup.lean:1399-1401), so "double point of S" = crossingPoint of a member of S (transverse conj. 2-3).

6. REVIEWER DISCREPANCIES. All are real as descriptions (noncrossing_arcs tautological alone; local 3 ≤ n; unprinted explicit fields; _hS unused; traced_curve inherited order; disjoint union on marks; ownership via conv:selected-visits pre-recorded at AUTHOR_NOTES.md:3232-3234 and the CV-DOM decision 3192-3297); none is blocking for the reasons above.
